RESEARCH UPDATED · 19 NOVEMBER 2026

The right storage box is the one you can fit, fill and lift. Really Useful 35L suits smaller groups of possessions; Strata Curve 65L provides more room for bulkier items. Here is what changes beyond the litre figure.

Really Useful 35L: our choice for sorting into manageable groups

A smaller box encourages you to separate categories rather than make one very heavy mixed container. That is useful for clothing, hobby supplies or possessions you take out regularly. The clips also give you a clear check that the lid has been fastened.

Customer feedback: an Argos review dated 16 November 2026 praises the handles for keeping lids attached during a move. Reviews on 13 and 14 November mention stacking, visibility and perceived sturdiness. Those are reports of use, not a certified load rating. Read Really Useful 35L customer feedback.

Why choose it: organised categories and a smaller individual container. Drawback: a bulky duvet or unusually shaped item may need a bigger box even when your total storage volume is modest.

Strata Curve 65L: our choice for bulkier storage

The 65L Curve is worth comparing for seasonal clothing or larger lightweight possessions. More capacity per box is useful only if the 60cm width fits your shelf, cupboard opening and route into storage.

Customer feedback: Argos owner comments describe useful visibility and stacking. A critical review dated 31 October 2026 reports a cracked lid and an insecure fit; another October reviewer found the lid initially difficult to clip. Inspect each lid and rim on arrival rather than assuming every delivered box will behave alike. Read Strata Curve 65L customer feedback.

Why choose it: storing bulky items without dividing them among several smaller containers. Drawback: extra volume makes overloading easier. A clipping lid should not be mistaken for a waterproof seal.

The capacity calculation that avoids a bad buy

The reviewed packs contain the same number of boxes, but one provides 105 litres of nominal capacity and the other 195 litres. That does not mean the larger pack is automatically better value. A box that will not pass through your cupboard door, or that is too heavy to lift when full, wastes its extra capacity.

To compare delivered cost, divide the pack price by the number of boxes first. Compare price per nominal litre only after checking fit and lid design. For books or tools, the useful limit may be the weight you can comfortably move rather than the litres available.

Measure before buying a multipack

  1. Measure the narrowest opening and the shelf depth, including hinges, pipes and skirting boards.
  2. Allow room above the box to release the lid. A box that fits tightly can still be difficult to open.
  3. Check usable internal dimensions if a particular object must fit. Tapered sides and handles reduce space; an external rectangle is not the internal storage area.
  4. Try one loaded box at a comfortable height before planning a tall stack. Put heavier items lower and follow the maker's load guidance.

Are either of these outdoor or food-storage boxes?

Do not choose either on the assumption that a clip-on lid makes it airtight, floodproof or suitable for loose food. Look for an explicit rating for the exact box if you need those uses. For ordinary indoor possessions, clear sides and a lid may be enough; damp sheds and long-term outdoor exposure call for different checks.

Our buying recommendation

Start with the Really Useful 35L format when you want categories you can retrieve individually. Choose the Strata Curve 65L when the possessions are bulky and the larger dimensions genuinely work. Buy fewer correctly sized boxes before committing to a large pack solely because its advertised litres look impressive.

How we researched this comparison

We compared the two named Argos products and their customer comments on 19 November 2026. Some Argos reviews carry incentive disclosures. These reports support the practical points discussed; they do not establish a failure rate or prove one plastic is stronger. We have not performed our own load or water-resistance tests. Pack sizes and live prices can vary between sellers.
